10 TOP TIPS TO CRUSH FPL 2026/27 ⚽💥

5-time Top 1k finisher Tom Freeman dropped his ultimate blueprint for hitting the ground running.

Here is your full Gameweek 1 cheat sheet before you hit lock 🚨

1️⃣ Play Your Own Game – Avoid early noise and knee-jerk FOMO. Recommendations often ignore your specific chip plan and team structure, so stick to your own vision.

2️⃣ Have a Plan... – Lock in your early chip strategy first (e.g., GW2 Bench Boost, GW4 Wildcard). Defining your strategy narrows down target players and eliminates draft paralysis.

3️⃣ ...But Don't Look Too Far Ahead – Keep primary focus tight on GW1–3, looking at GW5 at absolute maximum before the international break. A fast start is crucial in modern competitive FPL.

4️⃣ Bank Your Transfers – Hold onto free transfers whenever possible. Stacking transfers gives you maximum flexibility to jump on emerging form or fix multiple issues at once.

5️⃣ Limit Minutes Risks – Avoid overloading on rotation risks. If taking a punt on high-upside players, balance them with reliable 90-minute starters who have rock-solid xMins.

6️⃣ Prioritise Late Information – Be patient. Hold transfers until press conferences and team news are in—riding out early price rises is usually worth the extra clarity.

7️⃣ Study Pre-Season Tactics – Ignore friendly results and look at system setups. Watch for new manager shapes, inverted full-backs, wing-back usage, and dedicated set-piece routines.

8️⃣ Hunt Fixture Swings – Map out fixture turns early to jump on trends before your mini-league rivals (e.g., targeting Chelsea's run from GW4 or Fulham from GW6).

9️⃣ Know Your Set-Piece Takers – Set-piece output is more critical than ever. Prioritise players on corners, direct free-kicks, and penalties for high-floor, high-ceiling value.

🔟 Account for System Changes – Don't rely blindly on last season's data. A manager switch or club transfer drastically changes a player's role and defensive/offensive upside.
